metadata.purpose: Annotated fragment library for de novo assembly. Each pharmacophore records the target-engagement hypothesis its chemotype carries, so an assembled molecule inherits a predicted polypharmacology vector from its parts.
metadata.the_central_assumption: That a motif taken from a chemotype known to engage a target confers that engagement when transplanted onto a new scaffold. This is how medicinal chemists reason and it is wrong often enough to matter: activity depends on the whole molecule, not the fragment. Every engagement vector here is a hypothesis to be tested by assay, never a prediction of affinity, and no number in this file is a measured Ki, IC50, or EC50.
metadata.engagement_convention: Signed values in [-1,1] on the same directional scale the drug panel uses: negative means the motif drives the target's activity or the transcript down, positive means up. Downstream transcriptional consequences are listed alongside direct binding targets, matching the panel's target_effects convention, which is what makes assembled molecules scoreable against the disease signature.
metadata.attachment_points: '*' marks a bond to the rest of the molecule. Arms and caps carry one; linkers and scaffolds carry two or more.

roles.pharmacophore: carries a target-engagement hypothesis; the reason the molecule exists
roles.scaffold: multi-valent core that positions the arms
roles.linker: bivalent spacer setting distance and flexibility between arms
roles.cap: monovalent group tuning solubility, polarity, or metabolic stability; no engagement claim

metadata.sources: Chemotypes abstracted from published inhibitor and modulator classes named in each entry's parent_chemotype field.
metadata.scope: Fragments are disease-agnostic chemical matter and are shared across every campaign. The library began MS-oriented; Parkinson's pharmacophores were added when the PD profile reported ten of its fourteen targets as unreachable, and Alzheimer's when its profile reported six of fourteen (BACE1, PPARG, FYN, PTGS2, MAPK14, BCHE), and epilepsy when its profile reported ten of fourteen (SLC12A2, GABRA1, KCNQ2, SV2A, ADK, CACNA2D1, RPS6KB1, KCNQ3, P2RX7, CACNA1H), and Guillain-Barre syndrome when its profile reported seven of fourteen (C5AR1, SCN10A, SCN9A, TRPV1, KCNA1, C1S, P2RX3). unreachable_requirements() is the diagnostic that drives this file's growth.

evidence_schema.evidence_tier: strength of the published precedent that this chemotype engages its primary targets: approved_drug > clinical_candidate > published_chemotype > speculative
evidence_schema.primary_targets: the targets the chemotype is claimed to bind directly. Every other gene in `engages` is a downstream transcriptional consequence and is a materially weaker claim.
evidence_schema.claim_confidence: derived per fragment-target pair from the tier and whether the target is primary; see core/design/pharmacophores.Fragment.claim_confidence. It weights coverage scoring, so a speculative downstream claim contributes less than an approved-drug binding claim.
evidence_schema.why_this_exists: Without per-claim provenance a new scaffold assembled entirely from speculative downstream claims scores the same as one built on approved-drug pharmacology, and looks far more convincing than its evidence warrants.

fragments.name: Fumarate monoester Michael acceptor
fragments.note: Covalent KEAP1 cysteine modification releases Nrf2. The electrophile is the mechanism, so the resulting structural alert is intentional rather than a flaw.

fragments.name: Piperidinyl acrylamide covalent warhead
fragments.note: Targets the BTK Cys481 residue. In MS this is the one mechanism with both a B-cell and a microglial arm, which is why it dominates the progressive-disease pipeline.

fragments.name: 4-aminopyrimidine hinge binder
fragments.note: A donor-acceptor pair matching kinase hinge backbone. Deliberately promiscuous across the kinome: it buys potency and costs selectivity, and the engagement vector says so.

fragments.name: Sulfonylurea inflammasome blocker
fragments.note: Binds the NACHT domain and locks the inflammasome closed. Blocks IL-1beta maturation upstream, which is the only realistic small-molecule route to a secreted cytokine.

fragments.name: Picolinamide kinase headgroup
fragments.note: CSF1R blockade depletes and reprogrammes microglia. Depleting the resident immune cell of the CNS is a mechanism with an obvious ceiling on tolerability.

fragments.name: Aryl sulfonyl inverse-agonist arm
fragments.note: Occupies the RORgt ligand pocket and displaces the coactivator. Shuts down Th17 differentiation upstream of IL-17 rather than sequestering the cytokine.

fragments.name: Azetidine-3-carboxylic acid headgroup
fragments.note: A phosphate-mimetic head giving functional antagonism by receptor internalisation. The S1PR5 arm is the reason this class is argued to act on oligodendrocytes as well as lymphocytes.

fragments.name: 2-amino-1,3-propanediol headgroup
fragments.note: Requires sphingosine-kinase phosphorylation to become active, so this arm carries a prodrug dependency the assembled molecule inherits.

fragments.name: Hydroxamic acid zinc-binding group
fragments.note: Chelates the catalytic zinc. Potent and famously unselective across the metalloproteinase family, which is what sank the oncology hydroxamates; the CLDN5 term reflects barrier preservation rather than a binding event.

fragments.name: Acetamidine iNOS arm
fragments.note: Arginine-mimetic binding at the iNOS substrate site. Selectivity over the endothelial and neuronal isoforms is the whole difficulty of this class.

fragments.name: Adamantanamine open-channel blocker
fragments.note: Low-affinity, fast-off channel block: the kinetics are the reason memantine is tolerated where higher-affinity NMDA antagonists are not. The lipophilic cage also carries the molecule across the barrier.

fragments.name: Biguanide metabolic activator
fragments.note: Acts through complex-I inhibition and the resulting AMP:ATP shift rather than by binding AMPK. Strongly basic and polar, so it fights the CNS envelope hard.

fragments.name: Trifluoromethyl anilide
fragments.note: Blocks de novo pyrimidine synthesis, starving activated lymphocytes. Teratogenicity travels with the mechanism, not with the chemotype.

fragments.name: 3,5-dihydroxyheptanoic acid
fragments.note: An HMG-CoA transition-state mimic. Highly polar and acidic: a hard fit for a CNS envelope, and the reason brain-penetrant statins are the lipophilic ones.

fragments.name: Benzhydryl ether remyelination arm
fragments.note: M1/M3 antagonism releases the brake on oligodendrocyte-precursor differentiation. This is the only arm in the library pointed at the axis with no approved agent, and its anticholinergic burden is the cost.

fragments.name: Indole carboxylic acid
fragments.note: GPR17 arrests oligodendrocyte precursors mid-differentiation; antagonism releases them. Ligand pharmacology for this orphan receptor is still contested, so this is the least secure engagement claim in the library.

fragments.name: Resorcinol antioxidant arm
fragments.note: Sirtuin activation by polyphenols is mechanistically contested and confounded by assay-fluorophore artefacts. Included because the chemotype recurs in MS neuroprotection work, flagged because the evidence is weak.

fragments.name: Chlorophenyl TLR4 antagonist arm
fragments.note: Occupies the MD2 hydrophobic pocket. A lipophilic aryl group doing double duty as a permeability handle.

fragments.name: Aminothiazole apoptosis arm
fragments.note: Anti-apoptotic bias in neurons. The same bias in lymphocytes is a malignancy concern, and nothing in a small molecule makes it cell-type selective.

fragments.name: Methoxypyridine bioenergetic arm
fragments.note: A weakly-supported bioenergetic arm standing in for the NAD-precursor mechanism, whose actual pharmacology needs the intact nucleoside.

fragments.name: 1,3-disubstituted benzene
fragments.note: The default rigid two-arm core: cheap, flat, metabolically robust.

fragments.name: 1,4-disubstituted benzene
fragments.note: Maximum reach between arms; the most common bivalent spacer in medicinal chemistry.

fragments.name: 1,3,5-trisubstituted benzene
fragments.note: Three-arm core. Adding a third arm costs roughly 80-120 Da, which for a CNS envelope is most of the budget.

fragments.name: 2,4-disubstituted pyrimidine
fragments.note: Lowers logP relative to benzene and offers hinge-like acceptors; a standard kinase-programme core.

fragments.name: 1,4-piperazine
fragments.note: Adds sp3 character and a basic centre that helps solubility and hurts the CNS pKa term.

fragments.name: 1,3-disubstituted pyrazole
fragments.note: Small, polar, metabolically stable aromatic connector.

fragments.name: 1,4-piperidine
fragments.note: One basic nitrogen and one carbon attachment; raises fraction sp3 without a second basic centre.

fragments.name: Methylene
fragments.note: Shortest possible spacer; keeps the arms nearly in contact.

fragments.name: Ethylene
fragments.note: Two rotatable bonds bought for minimal mass.

fragments.name: Ether oxygen
fragments.note: Adds an acceptor and a bend without adding a donor.

fragments.name: Amide
fragments.note: Planar, rigid, and a donor-acceptor pair. Cheap to make and the most common bond in the pharmacopoeia.

fragments.name: Oxyethylene
fragments.note: Flexible polar spacer; each unit costs a rotatable bond.

fragments.name: Sulfonamide
fragments.note: Strongly polar and acidic-NH; adds a large TPSA increment that a CNS envelope may not afford.

fragments.name: Direct bond
fragments.note: No spacer: the arms are joined directly, giving the most rigid and lowest-mass connection.

fragments.name: Morpholine
fragments.note: Solubilising, weakly basic, and metabolically robust. The default polarity handle.

fragments.name: N-methylpiperazine
fragments.note: Strong solubility gain from a basic centre; costs the CNS pKa desirability term.

fragments.name: Dimethylamino
fragments.note: Small basic handle; a frequent site of oxidative N-dealkylation.

fragments.name: Methoxy
fragments.note: Low-cost acceptor; also a metabolic soft spot for O-demethylation.

fragments.name: Fluorine
fragments.note: Blocks a metabolic site for 18 Da and nudges logP and pKa.

fragments.name: Trifluoromethyl
fragments.note: Raises lipophilicity and blocks oxidation; heavy for what it does.

fragments.name: Methyl
fragments.note: The cheapest lipophilicity increment there is.

fragments.name: Hydroxyl
fragments.note: One donor and one acceptor; the CNS envelope charges heavily for donors.

fragments.name: Primary carboxamide
fragments.note: Two donors and an acceptor; strong solubility gain, strong CNS penalty.

fragments.name: Methylsulfone
fragments.note: Polar without being a donor, which is the combination a CNS envelope likes.

fragments.name: Cyclopropyl
fragments.note: Rigid sp3 lipophilicity; raises fraction sp3 cheaply.

fragments.name: 1,2,4-trisubstituted benzene
fragments.note: Three arms with two of them adjacent; the crowding is a real synthetic cost and a real conformational constraint.

fragments.name: 2,4,6-trisubstituted 1,3,5-triazine
fragments.note: Three symmetric arms on a polar, electron-poor core; each ring nitrogen is an acceptor, which lowers logP where a lipophilic three-arm design would otherwise overrun the envelope.

fragments.name: 2,4,6-trisubstituted pyridine
fragments.note: A trigonal core with a single basic nitrogen: one acceptor and a modest polarity gain over benzene.

fragments.name: LRRK2 aminopyrimidine hinge
fragments.note: Hinge-binding motif from the clinical LRRK2 series. The class liability is pulmonary phospholipidosis from peripheral LRRK2 inhibition, which a CNS-restricted design does not avoid.

fragments.name: Propargylamine MAO-B warhead
fragments.note: Forms a covalent adduct with the FAD cofactor. Irreversible inhibition means duration is set by enzyme resynthesis, not by pharmacokinetics.

fragments.name: Nitrocatechol COMT arm
fragments.note: The nitrocatechol is the pharmacophore and the liability at once: it chelates the catalytic magnesium, and nitroreduction is the suspected route to tolcapone's hepatotoxicity.

fragments.name: 2-aminotetralin dopamine agonist head
fragments.note: A rigidified dopamine mimic. Impulse-control disorders track with D3 affinity across this whole class.

fragments.name: Iminosugar glucocerebrosidase chaperone
fragments.note: An active-site chaperone that must bind tightly enough to stabilise folding and release in the lysosome. That inverted-affinity requirement is the whole difficulty of the class.

fragments.name: Bisindolylmaleimide-style kinase arm
fragments.note: Indole hinge binder. GSK-3beta sits upstream of tau phosphorylation, and selectivity against CDK family kinases is the recurring problem.

fragments.name: Dihydropyridine calcium-channel arm
fragments.note: Cav1.3 selectivity over Cav1.2 is the unsolved problem: isradipine failed phase 3 partly because the dose limited by peripheral vasodilation may never have engaged the CNS target.

fragments.name: Hydroxypyridinone iron chelator
fragments.note: Bidentate iron chelation. Brain-penetrant and, in deferiprone's case, capable of redistributing iron without systemic depletion -- though the phase 2/3 motor outcome was negative.

fragments.name: Ketoamide caspase warhead
fragments.note: Reversible covalent trap for the catalytic cysteine. Peptidomimetic caspase inhibitors have historically had poor exposure and little clinical success.

fragments.name: Tricyclic NOX2 inhibitor arm
fragments.note: Blocks microglial superoxide production. This chemotype is promiscuous across aminergic receptors, which is either an off-target burden or, in a dopaminergic disease, an outright hazard.

fragments.name: Aminopyrazole neurotrophic arm
fragments.note: The weakest engagement claim added for this disease. Small-molecule neurotrophin mimicry is contested throughout the literature, and the axis it serves has no approved agent precisely because nothing has worked.

fragments.name: Cyclic sulfonylamidine aspartyl-protease binder
fragments.note: The amidine engages the catalytic aspartate dyad. Four BACE1 programmes reached phase 3 and were stopped, two for worsened cognition, so the class carries a mechanism-based safety question that the fragment cannot resolve: BACE1 also processes substrates other than APP.

fragments.name: Thiazolidinedione PPAR-gamma head group
fragments.note: The acidic head group that anchors the ligand-binding domain. Pioglitazone failed phase 3 in mild cognitive impairment, so this is an approved-drug binding claim attached to a target whose benefit in this disease is unproven.

fragments.name: 4-Aminoquinazoline Src-family kinase hinge binder
fragments.note: Hinge-binding motif of the anilinoquinazoline series. Selectivity across the Src family is the recurring problem, and saracatinib did not slow decline in phase 2, so the target hypothesis is still unproven in patients.

fragments.name: Arylpropionic acid cyclooxygenase head group
fragments.note: The carboxylate that anchors the cyclooxygenase channel. It is also what limits brain exposure through efflux and ionisation, which is one reading of why NSAIDs failed the ADAPT prevention trial.

fragments.name: Pyridinylimidazole p38 hinge binder
fragments.note: The 4-pyridyl nitrogen binds the hinge. Early p38 inhibitors were repeatedly limited by hepatotoxicity and by tachyphylaxis, which is why the clinical case now rests on a brain-penetrant agent.

fragments.name: Dialkyl carbamate cholinesterase carbamylator
fragments.note: Carbamylates the catalytic serine of both cholinesterases. Butyrylcholinesterase activity rises as acetylcholinesterase falls with disease progression, which is the argument for engaging both.

fragments.name: N-Benzylpiperidine cholinesterase arm
fragments.note: The benzylpiperidine spans the gorge of acetylcholinesterase. Donepezil also binds sigma-1, listed here as a secondary claim.

fragments.name: Sulfamoylbenzoic acid loop-diuretic head group
fragments.note: The carboxylate and sulfonamide anchor the chloride-binding site. Both are ionised at physiological pH, which is why bumetanide barely enters the brain and why the neonatal trial did not answer whether NKCC1 inhibition in the brain helps.

fragments.name: 1,4-Benzodiazepin-2-one GABA-A positive modulator
fragments.note: Binds the interface between the alpha and gamma-2 subunits. Efficacy is limited by tolerance and by sedation, and alpha-subtype selectivity (alpha-1 for sedation, alpha-2 and 3 for anxiolysis) is the long-standing design problem.

fragments.name: Aryl carbamate Kv7 opener head group
fragments.parent_chemotype: Retigabine / ezogabine and the azetukalner series
fragments.note: The carbamate carbonyl H-bonds to the Kv7 pore tryptophan. Retigabine was withdrawn in 2017 because its secondary aniline dimerises into pigmented species in skin and retina, so a design that reproduces the free aniline reproduces the liability.

fragments.name: 2-Oxopyrrolidin-1-yl butanamide SV2A ligand
fragments.note: The pyrrolidone acetamide is the whole pharmacophore of the SV2A ligand class. Whether the ligand potentiates or inhibits SV2A function is not settled, so the sign of this engagement is a hypothesis.

fragments.name: 7-Deazapurine adenosine kinase inhibitor scaffold
fragments.note: An adenosine mimic. Adenosine kinase is the main sink for adenosine, so inhibiting it raises tone at the A1 receptor. The nucleoside-like series has poor drug-likeness and systemic toxicity, which is why no adenosine kinase inhibitor has been approved.

fragments.name: Gabapentinoid amino acid arm
fragments.note: A zwitterionic amino acid transported across the barrier by the L-type amino acid transporter, not by diffusion. That is unusual, and a designed molecule that lacks the transporter recognition motif may lose brain exposure even if it keeps affinity.

fragments.name: Piperazinyl pyrimidine S6 kinase hinge binder
fragments.note: Represents the piperazinyl-pyrimidine S6K1 series, described from the published chemotype rather than a specific compound. Selectivity over the AGC kinases is the recurring problem.

fragments.name: Adamantylmethyl amide P2X7 antagonist arm
fragments.note: The adamantane sits in a lipophilic allosteric pocket. The series is very lipophilic, so a design has to spend its property budget carefully. Brain-penetrant P2X7 antagonists have been tested in other indications, and none has shown efficacy in epilepsy.

fragments.name: Succinimide T-type calcium channel blocker
fragments.note: A small polar ring that blocks thalamic T-type channels and is first-line only for absence seizures. It has little activity against other seizure types, which makes it a narrow arm in a broad-spectrum design.

fragments.name: Aryl pyridone AMPA receptor antagonist arm
fragments.note: Binds an allosteric site on the transmembrane linkers and blocks channel gating. The class carries a boxed warning for psychiatric and behavioural effects, which the fragment cannot remove.

fragments.name: N-Acyl 2-arylpiperidine C5a receptor antagonist arm
fragments.note: The acylpiperidine holds the aryl and benzoyl groups in the receptor's allosteric pocket. Avacopan is approved for ANCA vasculitis and its hepatic enzyme elevations travel with the chemotype. Blocking the receptor leaves C5 cleavage intact, so it does not carry terminal complement inhibition's meningococcal risk in the same way.

fragments.name: Aryl sulfonamide Nav1.7 / Nav1.8 blocker arm
fragments.parent_chemotype: Aryl and acyl sulfonamide Nav1.7 inhibitors (PF-05089771 class)
fragments.note: The acidic sulfonamide binds the voltage-sensor domain of Nav1.7 with subtype selectivity. Isoform selectivity is the whole difficulty: non-selective sodium channel block would also hit nodal Nav1.6, whose loss impairs conduction, which is the wrong direction in a demyelinating neuropathy.

fragments.name: Indazolyl urea TRPV1 antagonist arm
fragments.note: The urea bridges the vanilloid pocket. Hyperthermia was the class-defining adverse effect of the systemic antagonists, and a design that reproduces the chemotype reproduces the liability.

fragments.name: 4-Aminopyridine Kv1 potassium channel blocker arm
fragments.note: Blocks exposed Kv1.1 channels at demyelinated nodes, restoring conduction. It is approved in MS to improve walking. The window is narrow: seizure is the dose-limiting toxicity, and the fragment is too small to carry selectivity.

fragments.name: Benzamidine serine-protease P1 group for C1s
fragments.parent_chemotype: Benzamidine-type C1s / trypsin-like serine protease inhibitors
fragments.note: The amidine sits in the S1 pocket that recognises arginine. C1s is the classical-pathway protease, and blocking it acts downstream of C1q. Trypsin-like proteases share the pocket, so selectivity is the recurring problem, and the strongly basic amidine limits permeability.

fragments.name: Diaminopyrimidine aryl ether P2X3 antagonist arm
fragments.note: P2X3 on sensory neurons is the ATP-gated channel behind the class's activity in cough and pain. Taste disturbance is the class-defining adverse effect. Approved in some regions for cough, not for neuropathic pain.
